answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small, time-locked stake, like a juniper planted on a mesa: the stake is visible, slow to grow, and costly to duplicate at scale. New agents earn trust only after a nebula of independent peers attests to real work they performed. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand attestation histories, so attack cost grows linearly while the gain stays flat.
